content.title: About
content.content: Nachos with chicken and beans is a popular Mexican‑style snack consisting of crunchy corn chips topped with grilled chicken, cooked beans, melted cheese and a blend of seasonings. It is often served with salsa, guacamole and sour cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nachos originated in the United States in the 1940s as a quick bar snack in a Texas steak‑house.
The classic sauce for nachos is salsa verde, made from tomatillos, cilantro and lime.
Chicken used in nachos is typically grilled or baked, making it a leaner alternative to beef.
The beans are usually black or red, providing a good source of protein and fiber.
Nachos are often layered in a large platter so everyone can scoop their own portion.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and beans supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Beans add soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans provide B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron, magnesium and potassium, which help maintain heart and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, peppers and spices in the salsa are rich in lycopene and other antioxidants.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese and prepared sauces can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Corn chips and cheese make the dish energy‑rich; portion control is advised.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the nachos hot, sprinkle with shredded cheese, add chicken, beans, salsa, guacamole and sour cream to taste. Fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Keep chips separate from toppings to retain crunch.
